title: Paya Soup

seo.title: How to Make Paya Soup — Easy Pakistani Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Paya Soup. This easy Pakistani recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Paya Soup — a beloved Pakistani classic

description: Paya Soup is a rich and hearty Pakistani delicacy, slow-cooked to perfection with tender lamb or beef trotters. This intensely flavorful broth, infused with aromatic spices, offers a warming and nourishing experience. It's a traditional comfort food often enjoyed during colder months or as a special occasion meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Trotters
instructions.text: Wash the cleaned trotters thoroughly. In a large pot, add the trotters and enough water to cover them. Bring to a boil, then drain the water completely. This step helps remove impurities and any strong odor.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot, heat oil over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and fry until they turn golden brown. Then add the ginger-garlic paste and sauté for another 2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Trotters
instructions.text: Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, black cardamoms, cinnamon stick, cloves, black peppercorns, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the pre-boiled trotters and whisked yogurt. Sear the trotters with the spices for 5-7 minutes, ensuring they are well coated.

instructions.title: Pressure Cook
instructions.text: Pour in 8-10 cups of water and add salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a boil. If using a pressure cooker, close the lid and cook for 45-60 minutes after the first whistle, or until the trotters are extremely tender. If using a regular pot, cover and simmer on low heat for 3-4 hours, checking water levels and stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Final Simmer and Seasoning
instructions.text: Once the trotters are tender and the gravy has thickened to your desired consistency, open the pressure cooker or remove the lid from the pot. Stir in the garam masala powder. Taste and adjust salt or spices if needed. Allow it to simmer gently for another 10-15 minutes without the lid to deepen the flavors.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Paya Soup into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander, sliced green chilies, and julienned ginger. Serve immediately with naan, roti, or plain rice for a complete and satisfying meal.

tips: To achieve a truly tender Paya, slow cooking is key. If you dont have a pressure cooker, cook on low heat for 3-4 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
For a richer flavor, you can lightly roast the whole spices (black cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns) before adding them to the oil.
Paya often tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Reheat gently on low heat, adding a little water if needed to maintain consistency.
